plan: Store a deep copy of the input dictionary in the constructor so the caller's data and the workspace state can never alias; return another deep copy from to_data().

Write one recursive walk generator yielding (item, parent_list, index) over the whole tree; reuse it for word counting, marker collection, and id lookup so traversal order and container rules live in one place.
Compute note word counts by first regex-substituting marker tokens [[?identifier]] with a space, then counting maximal \b\w+\b runs; add each reference's declared word_count.
Collect unresolved markers from note-text regex captures plus reference 'unresolved' lists into a set, returned sorted lexicographically.
Render the outline with a depth-carrying recursion: workspace title first, then '  ' * depth + '<kind>: <title>' per item, descending into section/group items at depth + 1.

Implement move as validate-then-mutate: check string ids, locate the item, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), reject non-containers, reject destination == item or destination inside the item's subtree (identity-based check), and bounds-check the insertion index — all before touching the tree, so any ValueError leaves state unchanged.
Perform the actual move as pop from the source parent list followed by append or insert into the destination list, preserving the item object and all descendants.
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at both API boundaries (constructor and to_data)
Single recursive walk generator yielding (item, parent_list, index)
Regex marker stripping before \b\w+\b word tokenization
Validate-then-mutate move protocol for failure atomicity
Identity-based subtree containment check against cycles
